articles.title: Signature Global-led consortium buys 194 acre land via auction for Rs 194 cr
articles.desc: A consortium led by Signature Global has successfully acquired 474.66 acres of land in Raigad, Maharashtra. The bid was valued at Rs 194 crore and enables the company to expand beyond Delhi-NCR. Signature Global will hold a 65 percent stake in the special purpose vehicle for this land. The management sees significant potential in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region property market.

articles.title: Sebi lowers margin requirements for agri-derivatives contracts
articles.desc: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has decided to lower the minimum margin requirements for agricultural commodities, reducing the initial margin to between 6% and 10%. This adjustment aims to align the margin standards for agricultural products with those for non-agricultural commodities, such as metals. Set to take effect on December 1, these new rules will be enforced for a year, with a potential extension based on market dynamics.

articles.title: BP launches offer to buy back up to $6 billion of bonds
articles.desc: BP is poised to execute a bond buyback strategy worth $6 billion, aiming to enhance its cash management. With oil price volatility in mind, the company is focused on maintaining a disciplined balance sheet. The bonds slated for repurchase are due from 2027 to 2034, primarily after 2030. Highlighting this effort, CEO Meg O'Neill stresses efficient debt management in light of the recent net debt reduction to $13.

articles.title: K Raheja Corp inks joint development agreement for 165-acre township in Mumbai region
articles.desc: K Raheja Corp has partnered with landowners to develop a large township in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. This joint development agreement covers a substantial 165-acre land parcel located at Panvel. According to CRE Matrix, the total value of the land is approximately Rs 956 crore. Revenue generated will be shared between K Raheja Corp and the landowners involved in the project.

articles.title: BlackRock raises its stake in Axis Bank to 5%
articles.desc: BlackRock has successfully increased its stake in Axis Bank to 5 per cent by acquiring more shares from the open market. Specifically, the investment giant procured 18,560 crore additional shares, nudging its ownership from 4.99 per cent. This elevates BlackRock's total holding to 155,726,461 shares. Notably, during the second quarter ending September 2026, Axis Bank showcased impressive growth, with a substantial surge in both net and operating profits.

articles.title: How new US chip restrictions on South East Asia will hit China
articles.desc: The new rules restrict chip exports and also access to their computing power, which China relies on heavily.

articles.desc: The project, covering National Highways 44 and 19, aims to improve connectivity and traffic efficiency along the corridor, which handles approximately 68,000 passenger car units (PCUs) daily, including freight, industrial, commuter and tourist traffic.

Centricity WealthTech launches private clients business for NRIs
articles.desc: Centricity WealthTech has launched its new global private clients business tailored for NRIs, aspiring to generate roughly Rs 60 crore in revenue by 2027-28. The company aims to elevate this target to an impressive Rs 400 crore annually within four years post-launch. To support this venture, more than 40 skilled private bankers have been recruited, addressing the surging demand for wealth management services among Indians residing abroad.

articles.title: M3M India to invest Rs 1,650 cr to build luxury homes under Jacob & Co brand in Gurugram
articles.desc: M3M India is set to invest Rs 1,650 crore in the luxurious M3M Jacob & Co Residences, located in the prime Sector 111 on the Dwarka Expressway in Gurugram. This lavish development will feature 120 exclusive apartments, each spanning about 7,300 square feet and starting at a price of Rs 26 crore.

articles.title: States' subsidy, cash transfer outgo jumps from 16% to 21% of revenue receipts in 5 years: Report
articles.desc: States' spending on subsidies and transfers has risen significantly over recent years and is expected to continue growing. By 2026-27, states are estimated to spend around 1 percent of GDP on cash transfer schemes. Major contributors to this increase are power subsidies and unconditional transfers for various beneficiaries, including women and farmers. States such as Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh are among the highest spenders in these categories.

articles.title: India, Philippines discuss defence, trade ties as PM Modi meets President Marcos Jr.
articles.desc: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. discussed enhancing cooperation in various sectors. They acknowledged the momentum in bilateral relations, particularly in defence and investment areas. The two leaders reflected on their previous meetings, emphasising the importance of their strategic partnership. India aims to expand its engagement with Southeast Asian nations through diverse initiatives.

articles.title: Indian bonds surge after oil slide eases aggressive rate hike concerns
articles.desc: On Tuesday, Indian government bonds rallied significantly, buoyed by falling oil prices that shifted market sentiment. The 6.94% 2036 bond's yield dipped to 7.2528%, a drop from 7.3169% the previous day. Analysts posit that lower oil prices could relieve inflationary pressure and bolster the rupee, alongside speculation of an upcoming RBI rate hike based on fresh inflation reports.

articles.desc: Rodríguez had denounced alleged links between criminal organisations and powerful figures in Costa Rica.

articles.title: Disney beats earnings forecasts, plans to increase content spending
articles.desc: In a promising financial update, Walt Disney has revealed a rise in quarterly revenue and earnings, attributed to greater theme park attendance and NFL broadcasts. Looking ahead, the company plans to elevate its content budget to $26 billion in the next fiscal year and raise its dividend by 33% to $2 per share.

articles.title: India's GDP growth pegged at 7.3% in FY26-27, may touch 7.7% next quarter: EAC-PM Chairman
articles.desc: India's GDP is expected to grow by 7.3% this financial year and 7.7% in the next quarter, S Mahendra Dev, Chairman of EAC-PM said. Sustained export momentum and improving foreign investment are crucial for this growth, he added.

articles.title: US government confirms investigation into tech firm Megaspeed
articles.desc: The Singapore-based company is suspected of helping to ship high-end AI chips from tech giant Nvidia to China, violating US export rules.

articles.title: Robust inflows, pullback in shorts lift rupee to seven-month peak
articles.desc: The Indian rupee saw a notable rise, achieving its peak value in seven months following a surge in foreign equity investments. Closing at 93.47 per dollar, this upswing was driven by an impressive influx of $10 billion this month. Additionally, traders observed substantial movements in the dollar-rupee non-deliverable forward market as bearish positions were unwound.

articles.title: Millions launches US stocks, ETFs investment facility for Indian investors
articles.desc: Investment platform Millions, operated by Raise Financial Services, has launched US stocks and ETFs on its app. This new feature allows Indian investors to make fractional investments and use systematic investment plans. The launch is supported by the International Financial Services Centres Authority under GIFT City's framework. Millions provides mutual funds, stocks, and zero brokerage, with no account fees or maintenance charges.

articles.title: Sebi may limit leveraged stock bets to curb volatility: Report
articles.desc: India's markets regulator is exploring potential limits on leveraged stock purchases amid increasing retail participation. Concerns have arisen as margin-funded stock bets have reached record levels in recent months. Discussions are ongoing regarding hard limits tied to a company's free float to manage risks effectively. While the regulator aims to mitigate market instability, it seeks to avoid disrupting retail investors' positions.

articles.title: Budget 2027: FM Sitharaman chairs third pre-Budget consultation with manufacturing sector leaders
articles.desc: Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the third pre-Budget consultation meeting for the Union Budget 2027-28 in New Delhi. The meeting included representatives from the manufacturing sector and senior government officials providing suggestions. This exercise aims to gather inputs from various economic sectors to shape the Budget's priorities. The Union Budget is scheduled for presentation on February 1, 2027, along with the Economic Survey.

articles.title: Odisha govt hikes Dearness Allowance by 3% for state employees
articles.desc: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced a three percent hike in Dearness Allowance for government employees. The increase raises the DA from 60 percent to 63 percent, effective from July 1. Pensioners will also benefit from the same three percent increase in Dearness Relief. Approximately 8.5 lakh government employees and pensioners will receive this additional financial support. Payments reflecting the increased DA will be included in the November salary.

articles.title: US AI chip curbs threaten Southeast Asia data centre boom, shares slump
articles.desc: The new rule restricts shipments of advanced chips to the region's major economies such as Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, which some Chinese companies have used to access computing power to train AI models. It also imposes new requirements on overseas data centres that supply "significant volumes of computing power" to firms headquartered in China.

articles.title: FIIs, MFs raise stakes in 5 largecap stocks for two straight quarters; shares rally up to 80%
articles.desc: FIIs and mutual funds have increased their stakes in five largecap stocks for two consecutive quarters, signalling rising institutional interest. All five stocks have delivered positive returns in FY27 so far, with gains ranging from 12% to 80%.

articles.title: Samsung Electronics, TSMC shares fall after US announces curbs on China's chip access

In the rush to go public before rival ChatGPT owner OpenAI, it has been caught in a volatility storm that's seen some $2 trillion wiped off AI chip giant and ubiquitous AI financier Nvidia's market value in just six weeks.

articles.title: India's CAD may touch 1.2% of GDP in FY27 as oil, gold demand pose risks: UBI
articles.desc: India's current account deficit is projected to reach 1.2% of GDP in FY27, driven by oil prices, according to a report by Union Bank of India. The report emphasizes that high crude oil prices and gold demand could impact the external balance. Merchandise trade deficit widened to a significant USD 39.88 billion in October. Additionally, imports surged while services trade surplus remained nearly flat during the same period.

articles.title: South Korean shares close at over 9-month low on Nvidia caution
articles.desc: South Korean shares experienced a significant decline of more than 2% amid concerns affecting chipmakers. The benchmark KOSPI closed at its lowest level since February due to persistent selling pressure. Foreign investors were noted as net sellers of shares worth approximately 1.4 trillion won. The Korean won weakened slightly against the dollar during this trading period. Additionally, South Korea's benchmark bond yields fell as market activities shifted.

Investors will scrutinise Data Center growth, hyperscaler demand, Blackwell and Rubin chip rollouts, margins and future guidance, alongside leadership uncertainty and rising costs, to assess its growth outlook.

articles.title: Australia sells A$6 billion of new 2057 Treasury bond
articles.desc: The Australian government's debt management arm made a significant move by issuing A$6 billion in a new Treasury bond set to mature in June 2057, boasting a yield to maturity of 5.62%. With bids totaling A$25.25 billion, investor interest remains strong. The settlement for this issuance is earmarked for November 24, with no additional issuances expected until March 2027. Five prominent banks took lead roles in this offering.

articles.title: Indian bonds gain as oil slide eases rate hike concerns
articles.desc: Indian government bonds saw an increase as oil prices dropped significantly in early trading. This decline in crude prices is expected to ease inflationary pressures and reduce concerns about aggressive rate hikes. The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield fell to 7.2813% during early trading hours. Lower oil prices are particularly beneficial for India, supporting the local rupee and current account deficit.

articles.title: JGB yields climb as buyers hold back on long-dated debt
articles.desc: Japanese government bond yields generally increased on Tuesday except for the benchmark 10-year yield, which fell. The 20-year and 30-year JGB yields reached their highest levels in about a month and since October. Investors are wary of taking interest-rate risks ahead of the 20-year bond auction. Concerns about falling equities may also affect bond supply-demand conditions amidst uncertainty.
